articles.title: Your Agentic Workflow's Cache Keepalive Costs 8x Too Much (v2: the interval frontier)
articles.summary: A cache keepalive is a common optimization for agent builders, but its setting can be wrong, costing up to eight times more than necessary. Measuring the economics of keepalives across various providers revealed that the ideal interval is four minutes, not 30 seconds. This finding suggests that keeping the cache warm only when the pause is longer than the provider's eviction point but shorter than its break-even horizon can save money for some users. The key takeaway is that the right interval depends on the provider and the agent's pause time, with a clean rule being to keep the cache warm in this window.

By providing a virtualized worktree, DeltaDB streamlines the process of working with multiple branches, enabling seamless collaboration and annotation.
